reasons: The lake identity record names Gerstein v. Pugh, court U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1975-02-18, year 1975.
The lake citation fields list official cite 420 U.S. 103, vendor-neutral cite 1975 U.S. LEXIS 29, and the same parallel citations: 95 S. Ct. 854, 43 L. Ed. 2d 54, and 19 Fed. R. Serv. 2d 1499.
The opinion frames the case as whether an arrested person is constitutionally entitled to a judicial probable-cause determination for pretrial restraint of liberty.
The opinion expressly treats arrest and detention standards as Fourth Amendment restraints on liberty, supporting a related placement under Seizure of the Person.
The opinion holds that the Fourth Amendment requires a judicial probable-cause determination as a prerequisite to extended restraint of liberty following arrest.

The opinion further states that the determination must be made by a judicial officer either before or promptly after arrest, supporting the anchor role for prompt probable-cause determination after warrantless arrest.
The disclosed text supports the core holding: "the Fourth Amendment requires a judicial determination of probable cause as a prerequisite to extended restraint of liberty following arrest."

The disclosed text supports the promptness and significant-restraint limits: the determination must be by a judicial officer before or promptly after arrest and as a condition for significant pretrial restraint of liberty.
The disclosed text supports the nonadversary point: adversary safeguards are not essential, and the Court reversed the decree requiring an adversary hearing.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For maximum precision, use "significant pretrial restraint of liberty" rather than "any extended pretrial restraint of liberty."
